thread:
emily: heads up — multiple customers reporting repeated 502/504s hitting hosted inference API since ~09:20 UTC. spike correlates with a lot of cold-starts for gpt-medium across eu-west. tickets: #CS-4129, #CS-4132. can we triage?
navid: on it. seeing surge in scale-up time in the autoscaler dashboard. KEDA is triggering, but pods are spending ~40-60s in Init/ContainerStart before readiness. gateway times out at 60s, so requests hit 504s. logs attached below.
emily: any idea why init is slow? images are cached on nodes.
jia: quick look at pod events — readiness probe failing repeatedly with: `readiness check failed: rpc: timed out waiting for auth handshake` and container logs show repeated attempts to contact auth-service with 503s.
sam: auth-service had a ~2m blip of 5xxs around same time — ops page shows a degraded deployment due to a config rollback that reduced max replicas. that made auth slower and caused token ops to queue.
ops-bot: deploy/rollout: service/auth rolled back to v1.8.2 by ci-cd at 09:12 UTC — reason: hotfix revert. monitor: 2xx dropped to 70% for 3m.
navid: so flow is: KEDA scales, new pods start, prestart init tries to fetch signing token/keys from auth-service, that call 503s causing init script to block -> readiness never becomes green -> HPA/KEDA think we still need more pods but gateway waits and times out. cascade.
lena: is this specific to gpt-medium? could be model init + auth request both in init path, doubling latency.
jia: yes model weight load also happens during init. two blocking calls stack. repro on dev: start a fresh pod while auth-service returns 503 for token endpoint -> pod init stays in `Init:0/1` for ~50s, readiness probe failing. paste logs:

```
[2026-03-15T09:21:14Z] init-script: requesting /auth/token -> 503 ServiceUnavailable
[2026-03-15T09:21:15Z] init-script: retrying auth token
[2026-03-15T09:21:18Z] model-loader: loading weights shard 3/12
[2026-03-15T09:21:40Z] readiness-probe: probe failed (exit 1)
```

support: customer-facing note: sending acknowledgement to customers and linking to status page. recommended workaround: switch to dedicated capacity or pin model to warm instances.
emily: immediate mitigations we can try:
- make init non-blocking: change prestart to fall back to anonymous token if auth fails for N seconds
- extend gateway timeout temporarily from 60s to 120s for affected routes
- increase readiness probe grace period and initialDelay on the deployment so model init + auth can finish
- scale up auth-service replica count back to previous level
navid: I can open the KEDA config, but we also should avoid aggressive re-scaling that floods nodes when pods don't become ready. Suggest changing `cooldownPeriod` to 30s and `pollingInterval` to 15s temporarily.
sam: ops can flip auth back to previous replica count; I'm invoking the rollback revert now. will post PR for the KEDA tweak.
jia: I'll PR a small change to init script to parallelize auth token fetch with weight loading (so auth delays don't fully block). but that's not instant.
lena: For a hotfix, let's patch the readiness probe to succeed if process is listening (not fully warmed) — then gateway can route and we can handle model warmups more gracefully. downside: might serve 502s if model not ready.
emily: customers asking for timeline. recommend: 1) ops revert auth capacity — 5-10m. 2) adjust KEDA polling/cooldown — 5m. 3) gateway timeout bump — 2m. 4) init non-blocking fix — next deploy.
support: telling customers ETA ~30m for mitigation steps. adding CS ticket updates.
ops-bot: action created: INC-2026 (ops) — revert auth capacity (assigned to sam)
sam: reverted auth replica count to 6 -> 200ms median auth token latency back to normal, verified. observing new pods passing readiness now.
navid: seeing scale lag drop from 52s -> 12s median for new pods. gateway 504s falling. monitoring for 15m.
emily: great. postmortem items: remove blocking auth call from init path, add circuit-breaker and faster fallback, tune KEDA cooldown and polling, consider pre-warming policy for sudden bursts. I'll write initial incident writeup.
support: customers updated, closing escalation loop once metrics stable 30m. :thumbsup:
